task.description:
Повторная проверка (раунд 2) части REQ-001 проекта docs/design/REQ-001-pixel-office.md после доработки проектировщика (версия 2; его отчёт — step-01-code-designer-r2.json, 35 записей result.changes). Проверьте сами, не по отчёту: (1) каждая ваша находка C1–C10 — исправлена или нет, с вашими доказательствами; особенно C1 (протокол опроса страницы: таймаут запроса, один запрос в полёте, проверка from == entries.length) — повторите свой случай с остановленным сервером (SIGSTOP) на новых тестах PG-14b/c/d; C2 и C3 — проект выровнен точно по исправленному тексту критерия 6(г) и списков «Что меняется» (требования прошли шаг 00b раунд 5); C4–C9; (2) новое содержание версии 2: решения D11–D14, пробы P20, восемь случаев PG-12d6, мутанты M41–M44 — проверьте, что случаи различают неверные реализации, как заявлено; (3) раздел 10 по-прежнему отображает все 14 критериев REQ-001 на существующие тесты, нет кода реализации, write set внутри объявления ORCH; (4) нет новых дефектов. Решение ORCH по пункту 14 раздела 13 — в context.orch_rulings.

ОГРАНИЧЕНИЯ ПРИ ПЕРЕПРОВЕРКЕ ПРОБ. Пробы с настоящей сессией Claude Code (claude -p …) тратят лимит владельца: не больше одной такой пробы на вас, с самым коротким запросом и --max-budget-usd 0.5; остальное — без модели. Не пишите в ~/.sai-pixel-office и в настоящие настройки (~/.claude, sai/.claude/settings.json): временная папка с подменой HOME. Не запускайте ничего на порту 4780; нужен сервер — свободный порт. В этой оболочке нет `timeout`: оборачивайте команды на node или perl.
acceptance_criteria: each of your round-1 findings resolved/open with evidence
new findings with design section, severity, concrete fix
commands run and URLs opened listed (bounded)

result.summary:
VERDICT: PASS. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, WF-02 step 1b, round 2, REQ-001 part. All ten round-1 findings (C1-C10) are resolved, each with my own evidence below; I found no new blocking defect. Nine non-blocking notes (n1-n9) are at the end; n1 (three missing cases for the main-session row) should go into TEST-DESIGNER's task or the design, ORCH's choice. I made no live model call (the one allowed probe was not needed: the only new live-dependent claim, P18, was re-derived from the designer's raw stream), wrote nothing to ~/.sai-pixel-office, ~/.claude or sai/.claude/settings.json, and did not touch port 4780 (my servers used 47894-47899 and ephemeral ports; all stopped, no Chrome left).

OBJECT. docs/design/REQ-001-pixel-office.md v2, sha256 e09f763146e274e55bfad577b46d9bad36ded6126b2d31335b5845b943ba4c84, 2888 lines, mtime 16:42:50 local (unchanged during my run). I read all of it. The designer's backup REQ-001-v1-backup.md is byte-identical to the v1 I validated in round 1 (sha256 176f4ee3...3f96), so I diffed v1 to v2: 56 hunks, 235 lines removed, 906 added; every removed line is replaced or updated, nothing was dropped silently, and every hunk belongs to one of the 35 change entries of step-01-code-designer-r2.json. docs/requirements.yaml sha256 de702d1909e0de5f446a1cad87f6a3d0364aa53acbb1b02b22d0fe8c69d4dd8c, 640 lines (the file REQ-VALIDATOR r5 passed); with the status line restored to pending, the P20 commands give REQ-001 530b1c3b13d58598ebb77ef50e60e42bb518654650423d7b20b39fdc416d4e21 and REQ-007 d842c5983085e38796e939fb6af7dc0bad5fa4225772fe96070377e578f1ead5, equal to §0 and §11 Q1. Sections 4.3-4.5, D11, D13 and the office parts of §3.6-3.8 belong to the other validator; I read them only for consistency with REQ-001.

ROUND-1 FINDINGS, ONE BY ONE
C1 (poll protocol) - RESOLVED. Text: §4.6 now has one request in flight, a 3 s AbortController timeout counted as a failure, a cursor of entries.length (not the response's lines), a response applied only when from is 0 (replace) or entries.length (append), otherwise dropped with one immediate re-poll (a second inconsistent response in a row is a failure), a response-shape check, an immediate poll on visibilitychange; §2.3 (env with setTimeoutFn, AbortControllerCtor), §8.3 E26/E26b, D12, tests PG-14b/c/d. My own evidence: (a) I wrote the protocol from the text (scratch, not project code) and ran it against a real server that I stopped with SIGSTOP and resumed with SIGCONT, real timers and real fetch. Correct implementation: SIGSTOP at 4.52 s; «Нет связи» shown at 9.06 s (3 s after the request that started at the 6 s tick, i.e. at most POLL_MS + 3 s after the stop); SIGCONT at 11.02 s; message cleared at 11.04 s; at the end the page held 20 entries = the server's 20 lines, no duplicates, contiguous, 8 fetch calls. The round-1 behaviour (no timeout): at 10.5 s, 6 s into the stop, no message and the page looked live (entries 9, one request hanging). (b) I wrote PG-14b, PG-14c, PG-14d (plus PG-13 and PG-14) as described in §10.2 on the fake environment of §10.1 (manual clock, fetch that never settles and rejects on abort, document with visibilityState) and ran them on the correct implementation and six wrong ones: correct passes all; no timeout (M31) fails PG-14b; wrong from applied (M32) fails PG-14c; no one-in-flight rule fails PG-14b and PG-14d; no visibility poll fails PG-14d; cursor = response lines fails PG-14c (needs a gap response whose lines differ from entries.length, which PG-14c's 'пропущенный' case provides); no immediate re-poll fails PG-14c. Two small points are in n2 and n3. Residual, informational (n7): the first load also has the 3 s limit.
C2 (6(г)) - RESOLVED. The amended criterion 6(г) reads (requirements.yaml line 270): a row without an end of answer is closed as «окончание не записано» at the next request of the same session or a session end after its start, and if neither, at a server start after its start (as for tasks in (в)); a row closed only by a server start stays open for the end of the answer, which closes it later as «завершена»; an end of answer without an open row changes nothing; the «Проверка:» names request -> server start -> end of answer. Design §4.2 (first trusted event of session S after i decides; only if none, a server start with journal_lines > i), §3.5 (closed_by server_start, end_index), §1.1 hook table (Stop), §9.4 item 7 and PG-12d6 case (1) say the same thing. My evidence: I wrote two independent implementations (the design's first-event rule; an event-driven reading of the amended text only) and compared them on 8,000 random journals (two sessions, resumes, session ends, untrusted lines, 0-3 server starts) at every prefix: 68,001 comparisons, 0 differences; the stale record is covered by case h. I then built the eight PG-12d6 cases from their catalogue text (not from P20): my results equal P20's table line by line. I also re-ran the designer's own P20 script (probe21/mainrow.mjs): its output is unchanged. Mutants as I implemented them: M41 differs from the rule on (2) b1, b2, b3, and on (3) c1 only when the fixture carries the current server's start record, as P20's does (its c1 has a start with journal_lines 0; with no start record at all, case (3) would not separate M41, and (2) still does; the catalogue text of (3) should say that the start record is present); M42 on (3) c1, c2; M43 on (1) a2, the late Stop (the named scenario alone catches only M43, as the designer says); M44 on (4) and (5); M18 on (2) b2, the clock-behind case. So each named wrong reading is separated by the named cases, as claimed. Further wrong readings are not separated: see n1.
C3 (helper in the write lists) - RESOLVED. Both «Что меняется» lists (REQ-001 lines 201-206, REQ-007 lines 612-619) name tools/test/pixel-office-helpers.js and keep «прежние тесты, в том числе tools/test/helpers.js, не меняются»; design §10.1, §13.1, §14 and the TEST-DESIGNER row follow. Measured by me on a full copy of the current tree (npm ci state, fake HOME): baseline npm run check exit 0, 115/115, skipped 0, todo 0; with a helper whose top level has a failing test, npm test (node --test "test/**/*.test.js") still exits 0 with 115/115, while a bare node --test runs it (117 tests, 1 fail, exit 1); a mis-formatted helper makes format:check exit 1, an unused variable makes lint exit 1, an inline /* eslint no-undef: 0 */ makes the criterion-14 directive grep find it (exit 0 = check fails as intended); the fake HOME holds only .npm. The criterion-14 pins reproduce on the live tree: items 2 (true), 3 (5c592925...edf0a4), 4 (92d27c4e..., cd446cc5..., 4d56952b...), 5 (exit 1), 6 and 7 with -name '*.*js' (856ee001..., bec0f88d...), 8 and 10 (exit 1).
C4 (names) - RESOLVED: MainRow.key = 'main:' + start_index (§3.5, PG-12d7), the table event kind -> role/description for the journal row (§3.5, PG-23), data-key from Task.key and MainRow.key (§4.7).
C5 (stale journal_lines) - RESOLVED: §3.4 and §4.2 ignore a start record whose journal_lines exceeds the number of lines (the response's lines, on the page entries.length), E33, README limitation 11, PG-12c7, M37, D14. My case h (one line, record with journal_lines 5) leaves the row in progress with the rule and shows unrecorded without it. Residual, informational: if the journal later regrows past the stale count the old record applies again; README tells the owner to delete both files together.
C6 (busy port) - RESOLVED: E12, SV-11b-e. I re-ran P14: silent socket gives TimeoutError after 1006 ms, closed connection 3 ms, text 9 ms, JSON without app 2 ms, other app 2 ms, the real answer is recognised.
C7 (unreadable journal) - RESOLVED: §2.2 (starts() and lineCount() raise JournalReadError except on ENOENT), §5.2, E31, SV-44. I re-ran P13: readFileSync gives EACCES (chmod 0000) and EISDIR (directory; openSync on a directory succeeds), ENOENT for a missing file; appendFileSync gives EACCES on a 0400 file and EISDIR on a directory: exactly the design's table.
C8 (HMAC key) - RESOLVED: §2.2 and HK-16 fix the key as the 43-character string in UTF-8 and the signature as lowercase hex, with a known answer. I computed it: Node createHmac and openssl dgst both give 4b10787ad84cb619fbc717640b635f24477c05db51a4e2066eb6a700ae6231d5 for the 93-byte body; the base64url reading gives e3d5648ae8be..., so HK-16 tells them apart.
C9 (six small items) - RESOLVED: (i) §1.2 item 1 is now the same rule as §4.2(з); (ii) Task.session_id is the session of the last SubagentStart, rule (в) uses it, PG-12c8; (iii) §4.1 and README items 9 and 10 name the clock assumption and the hidden tab; I re-ran P19 (1, 1, 28, 217 real lines marked for 100, 150, 600, 3600 s on the designer's generator) and measured with my own generator and implementation: 0-2, 29, 222 at a 15 s mean gap and 47, 832, 6,227 at 0.56 s, the same orders; (iv) --dir without SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR: warning text in §9.1, §6.2, README item 12, SV-45; (v) the eslint block is in the REQ-001 page row of §14 and the step order puts layout and office-* before app.js; (vi) PROMPT has run_in_background true: I re-derived P18 from the raw stream (2.1.286): the Agent tool_input has run_in_background true, tool_response status async_launched, hook_response counts SessionStart 2 (two probe handlers), UserPromptSubmit 2, Stop 2, SubagentStart 1, SubagentStop 1, PostToolUse 1, two result messages, and the §1.8 jq commands run on that stream give 'Async agent launched successfully...' and the session id; the sub-agents page (fetched again today, identical to my round-1 copy) says that with fork mode off, as in -p, Claude runs a subagent in the background by default and in the foreground when it needs the result.
C10 (process) - RESOLVED as a handover: ORCH writes the decision record (D1-D8 and D10-D14; D9 is in the requirement) after this PASS and before BACKEND-DEV; DOC-UPDATER takes the seven anti-pattern entries of §11 Q13. §12 says so. ORCH's rulings (item 14 of §13: office parts of app.js, index.html, texts.js, style.css count as «файлы офиса»; no clause for O1) are consistent with the design (n5).
HARDENING PROPOSALS - ADOPTED: step T item 12 (grep for /* global x */): it finds /* global document */, /*globals window*/ and /* global */, not /* globally */, exits 1 on the existing dirs (2 until tools/src/pixel-office exists); HK-17 and threat T13 (HOME and SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR in a temp dir for every spawned process) with the optional real-journal hash (item 13); PG-20 purity rules. The criterion-14 commands are unchanged.

NEW CONTENT OF V2
D12 and D14 match §4.6 and §3.4. D11 (28 desks) and D13 (label rule) are REQ-007's; they do not contradict REQ-001 or REQ-007's 'не меньше 24'; I re-ran the designer's grid generator (P16: 27 x 24, 28 desks, 112 desk cells, 438 floor cells, 756 ordered pairs, longest path 37 cells, 0 problems) and counted 23 files in .claude/agents with a longest name of 49 characters, as D11 and D13 say; I did not re-measure the label widths (P15), which is the other validator's. P20: its three commands are reproduced as described (the first by my own implementations above; the second and third by me, see C3 and the hashes). The U3 recipe of §10.4 (new): I ran it as a bash script against my own stand-in pages under the §5.4 policy: the good page passes conditions 1-5 in 2 s with no Chrome process left; a page whose drawing throws after the task list fails conditions 4 and 5 (the old U3 would have passed it); a classic <script src> with import fails 2-5 (SyntaxError); a <style> element fails 5 (CSP line); a closed port ends after 31 s with 'НЕ ПРОЙДЕНО' and no process left. P12, P13, P14, P18, P19 re-checked as above; P17's CSP findings reproduced by these runs.

STILL CONFIRMED
(3a) Section 10.3 maps all 14 REQ-001 criteria to tests, commands or steps, and the sub-items of each criterion are covered; my script over the catalogue (145 rows) and sections 3, 4, 7, 8, 10.3, 10.6, 11-14 and both appendices finds 0 unresolved test IDs, 44 mutants numbered 1-44, 34 well-formed tables. The named scenario of 6(г) is PG-12d6 case (1) and the helper is in 14. (3b) No implementation code: no function/const/=>/import/class/await constructs; only shapes, tables, the grid, the settings form, UAT commands and probe logs. The multi-line shell of the U3 recipe is a verification step like U1's command, not product code (n9). No TBD or deferral language outside §13. (3c) Write set: every path of §14 is inside the declared paths of PO-20260930-01 (parallel-runs.jsonl lines 1 and 3, unchanged); snapshot.js, cli.js, .claude/agents, docs/business-plan are not touched. (3d) Quality bar: all 17 rows (Q1-Q14, R1-R3) present, N/A rows with reasons. (3e) Security (§7) unchanged apart from T13; no recorded decision contradicted. (3f) Step T is still executable (see C3).

NEW FINDINGS, ALL NON-BLOCKING
n1 [MEDIUM] §10.2 PG-12d6 and §10.6. Three plausible wrong readings are separated by none of the eight cases or by PG-12d1-d5: the next request of ANOTHER session closes the row; a SessionEnd of ANOTHER session closes it; a SessionEnd of the same session BEFORE the request closes it (resume). I implemented them against my rule: 'next request of any session' is not caught by any of the cases; neither are the other two. The criterion's own words ('следующем запросе той же сессии', 'после её начала') call for the tests, and two parallel sessions in sai/ are realistic. Fix (either in the design or as mandatory cases for TEST-DESIGNER): (9a) [request S1, request S2] -> both rows «обрабатывает запрос»; (9b) the same after a server start -> the S1 row «окончание не записано» with closed_by server_start (not next_prompt); (10) [request S1, SessionEnd S2] -> S1 stays «обрабатывает запрос»; (11) [SessionEnd S1, SessionStart S1, request S1] -> the row is «обрабатывает запрос»; mutants M45 next request of any session closes, M46 SessionEnd of any session closes, M47 any earlier SessionEnd closes. I ran these cases: both reference implementations agree on the expected results and the three wrong readings differ on them.
n2 [LOW] §10.2 PG-14b says 'счётчик вызовов fetch за 3 тика не растёт'; with a 2 s tick and a 3 s limit only one interval tick fits inside the request. Say: 'tick' = a call of the interval callback; the request starts at a tick, three calls of the callback and the tick at +2 s send nothing, the abort comes at +3 s, the message appears, the tick at +4 s resumes. (My rendition uses exactly this.)
n3 [LOW] §10.6 lists M31 and M32 for the new protocol; my matrix shows PG-14b/c/d also catch 'no one-in-flight rule', 'no visibility poll', 'cursor = lines' and 'no immediate re-poll'; add them as mutants so TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR applies them.
n4 [LOW] §1.1 (lines 132-134): 'строка закрывается следующим запросом или концом сессии' omits the server start of the amended 6(г); add 'или запуском сервера'.
n5 [INFO] §13 item 14 still asks ORCH to confirm; ORCH has ruled (r2 context): record 'подтверждено ORCH'.
n6 [INFO] §2.1 file listing omits tools/test/pixel-office-helpers.js (it is in §10.1 and §14).
n7 [INFO] §4.6: the first full load also has the 3 s limit. Measured here (Node fetch plus JSON.parse, server stringifying parsed lines, about 390 bytes per line): 100,000 lines 0.33 s, 300,000 1.2 s, 600,000 2.6 s, 1,000,000 5.1 s; above roughly 700,000 lines the page could never load. At the journal growth of hundreds of lines a day that is years away and the requirement fixes 100,000 as the scale, but one README line or a longer first-load limit would make it explicit.
n8 [LOW] §8.3 E27 and PG-19 say invalid elements are 'пропущены'. Make it explicit that they stay in entries as null (length and indices unchanged), and assert in PG-19 that the next request uses after = entries.length; filtering them out would shift every index and make the next poll re-send lines.
n9 [INFO] The header line 'CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR версию 2 ещё не проверял' becomes stale after this verdict; the multi-line U3 recipe is judged a verification step (see above).
